hook_text: Same pulley, same rope, same bucket. Hang the pulley from the bucket instead of the beam and the pull halves.
clip_script: Tie the rope to the beam. Run it down round a pulley, hang the bucket from the pulley, pull up on the free end. The pulley rides up the rope with the load. Now count the rope sections holding the bucket: two, one to the beam, one to your hand. One rope, one tension, so each holds half, and you pull half. 20 newton bucket, 10 newton pull. Mechanical advantage 2. Rule for every pulley system: count the supporting sections. The price: 600 millimetres of rope for a 300 millimetre lift. You will measure about 1.8, because you lift the pulley too and fight its axle. And you are pulling upwards, which is awkward. Next: a fixed pulley on top turns it round.
visual_style: Whiteboard beam, rope down round a pulley on a bucket, up to a hand; two rope sections highlighted with half-load labels; a balance reading 10; a distance ratio 600 to 300.
pacing: Rig it, count two, halve it, pay in rope, the honest 1.8, the awkward direction.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and lift a book with a loop of string in both hands to feel the halving.
